item: The allocator reading says what glibc did with the variable: the first accepted of two entries, a plain decimal number, nothing under a malloc replacement the process loaded or an arena-limit tunable (the Opus reads of #1304 and of its fix)
key_paths: src/monitoring/session_hwm.py; src/monitoring/soak_window.py; scripts/launch.sh; tests/test_malloc_arena_default.py; docs/CHANGES.md; docs/ledger/RULINGS_INDEX.md; docs/ledger/LESSONS.md
summary: The read of R114 (#1304, merged before it ended) ran glibc 2.39 itself with crafted environments and found that the allocator setting each session records could say the opposite of what the allocator did. A variable named twice reads as its FIRST value, which is the one glibc and os.environ apply (8 then 1 gives 8 arenas; the reading said capped at 1, and the test pinned that wrong order). A number counts only in the plain decimal form glibc reads the way a person does (leading blanks or tabs allowed; 4 followed by a space, 08, 010, 0x4, a non-ASCII digit and a 23-digit number are each not claimed, and read as not known). GLIBC_TUNABLES naming glibc.malloc.arena_max outranks the variable and reads as not known; a preloaded jemalloc, tcmalloc or mimalloc has no glibc arenas and reads as not capped (the read of the fix then judged this by what the process LOADED, not by the name LD_PRELOAD gives); an empty starting environment is an env -i start and no longer falls back to os.environ; arena_cap names only a cap the process runs with. The soak window's memory-guard block now carries the setting when the guard's own state cannot be read (its fourth early return), the launcher's comment and the changelog no longer say freed memory stays in its own thread's arena, and a launcher test pins that an install file that unsets or empties the variable, or a caller that passes it empty, still gets the default. A new test starts a child through execve with the variable named twice and counts the arenas glibc kept (it skips where nothing creates per-thread arenas); the Windows lane's path comparison in the starting-block fake uses as_posix. Fifteen mutations of the reading, the launcher's order and the soak window are each caught. The read of that fix, at 87e5284e, ran the same child again and found the reading still judging by names. A preload counted as a replacement because LD_PRELOAD named one, though a path that is not there loads nothing and the cap holds (and a replacement loaded through a symlink under another name is one): the reading now asks what the process loaded, from /proc/self/maps, and says not known where the map cannot be read (dladdr(malloc) was tried and answers python3 for every allocator). A variable named twice applies its first ACCEPTED value, so a first value glibc ignores (4 followed by a space) lets the second apply and reads as not known. GLIBC_TUNABLES is parsed in every copy and a semicolon is no separator there (the tunable's value is invalid, so it is ignored and the variable applies). tbbmalloc alone, which a threading runtime may load, is no replacement; tbbmalloc_proxy is. The launcher's comment says what happens to a freed chunk (above about 1 KB it goes back to the arena that owns it, a smaller one waits in the freeing thread's cache). Checked against a real glibc child over 29 environments, against a real jemalloc and a symlinked one where the machine has one, and against a stand-in library the loader really loads (named like an allocator, defining no malloc) for the file the reading follows. The coordinator's check of the fix then found the table's row for a negative number wrong: glibc reads the value with strtoul, which takes a sign, so -2 is the largest number there is and a cap that bounds nothing (named first, it keeps all 17 arenas with 2 behind it), where the row had said glibc ignores it. Three CPUs or more cannot tell the two apart (both keep 17), and below that glibc's default limit (8 arenas per CPU) bites and a cap that bounds nothing keeps more than the default does, so the rows that expect glibc to have applied such a cap now compare with what a huge valid cap keeps, the rows that expect it ignored compare with the default, and each ignored value is proved ignored by naming it first with a bounding value second, which tells them apart anywhere. The reading is unchanged: it does not claim a signed number and says not known. Fifty-four mutations of this read's fixes and of the coordinator's check of them (the allocator reading's, the release run's and the search-timing report's) are each caught. Lesson: LESSONS.md, A READING OF ANOTHER PROGRAM'S BEHAVIOUR IS TESTED BY RUNNING THAT PROGRAM, NOT BY AGREEING WITH THE CODE.
